lessons.title: Build Chat Messages
lessons.description: Implement chat_messages(system, user) returning list of role/content dicts. The test checks that chat_messages('sys', 'hi')[0]['role'] equals 'system'; chat_messages('sys', 'hi')[1]['content'] equals 'hi'.
learning_objectives: This step reads the role of the first message, using messages holding role.
lessons.solution_code:
def chat_messages(system, user):
    return [{'role': 'system', 'content': system}, {'role': 'user', 'content': user}]

tests.name: test_chat_messages
tests.unittest_code:
def test_chat_messages(self):
    m = chat_messages('sys', 'hi')
    self.assertEqual(m[0]['role'], 'system')
    self.assertEqual(m[1]['content'], 'hi')

lessons.title: Practice Few-Shot Packing
lessons.description: Implement few_shot(examples, query) formatting Input/Output blocks then the query. The test checks that few_shot([('2+2', '4')], '3+3').endswith('Output:') is true; few_shot([('2+2', '4')], '3+3') contains 'Input: 2+2'.
learning_objectives: This step counts the packed examples, using shots holding kelp.

tests.name: test_few_shot
tests.unittest_code:
def test_few_shot(self):
    text = few_shot([('2+2', '4')], '3+3')
    self.assertIn('Input: 2+2', text)
    self.assertTrue(text.endswith('Output:'))

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Text Sequence Type str — join/formatting to assemble prompt blocks

lessons.title: Ask for JSON
lessons.description: Implement json_instruction(schema_keys) telling the model to return JSON with those keys. The test checks that json_instruction(['name', 'age']) contains 'name'; json_instruction(['name', 'age']) contains 'age'; json_instruction(['name', 'age']) contains 'JSON'.
learning_objectives: This step reads the ok flag from the JSON object, using blob holding ok.

tests.name: test_json_instruction
tests.unittest_code:
def test_json_instruction(self):
    s = json_instruction(['name', 'age'])
    self.assertIn('name', s)
    self.assertIn('age', s)
    self.assertIn('JSON', s)
